SP-1.outcome: A fresh clone of the public repo installs, builds and passes verify; every source has a license and compatibility route; the 93-entry manifest validates; the kit-only guard rejects violations.

The tracked compatibility matrix records the four source licenses with primary-source URLs and public-redistribution verdicts, the 22 enhancement routes, the 7 capability routes, exact pinned versions and one notification-engine ruling.

# Plan — Personal UI kit package with a public catalog

Skeleton (collaborative planning, phase Esqueleto). Milestones and subplans only; tasks are defined subplan by subplan with the owner.

Approach.text:
## Approach
Public npm-workspaces monorepo `dav033/david-ui`: `packages/ui` is `@dav033/david-ui` (GitHub Packages, Changesets + Actions), `apps/catalog` is the public Next.js 16 catalog on Vercel that consumes the package through the workspace. Package first; the catalog follows and every later family lands in package and catalog together. Missing pieces the catalog needs are added to the package in the same change (R4). D-003.

M1 — Package foundation: monorepo, ident.text:
### M1 — Package foundation: monorepo, identity and publishing
The public monorepo passes npm run verify, the package publishes to GitHub Packages from a merged changeset, and a fresh Next 16 + Tailwind 4 app installs it and builds with the kit theme.

- **SP-1 — Public monorepo, toolchain, license and compatibility ruling, manifest and kit-only guard**: A fresh clone of the public repo installs, builds and passes verify; every source has a license and compatibility route; the 93-entry manifest validates; the kit-only guard rejects violations. Covers R1, R2, R4, R5, R10, R11.

  SP-1 tasks (draft for owner confirmation). Owner rulings 2026-10-26 (SPEC Clarifications SP-1): (A1) no open-source LICENSE file, all rights reserved: README states personal use and every `package.json` says `"license": "UNLICENSED"`; (A2) agents commit directly to `main` and the integrated `main` is pushed to `origin` (owner-authorized production action, SPEC Constraints). Inputs: `gh` logged in as dav033 with `repo` and `workflow` scopes; no other SP-1 input.
  Contracts produced: toolchain@1 (T1), upstream-compat@1 (T2), dependency-set@1 (T3), catalog-manifest@1 (T4), kit-only-guard@1 (T5). Integration test T6, audit T7. DAG: T1 → T2 → T3 → {T4, T5} → T6 → T7.
  Verifier facts the tasks must respect: snapshots hold tracked and untracked files but never ignored output; before each check the verifier runs `npm run build --workspaces --if-present`; `node_modules` is mounted from the lockfile; there is no `.git`, home directory or `.env`.

- [ ] T1 — Create the public repository dav033/david-ui with a root commit and scaffold the npm-workspaces monorepo toolchain · repo: app · verify: `npm run build` · files: package.json, package-lock.json, .gitignore, .node-version, tsconfig.base.json, eslint.config.mjs, vitest.config.mts, playwright.config.ts, README.md, .github/workflows/ci.yml, packages/ui/package.json, packages/ui/tsconfig.json, packages/ui/tsconfig.build.json, packages/ui/src/kit-info.ts, packages/ui/src/kit-info.test.ts, apps/catalog/package.json, apps/catalog/tsconfig.json, apps/catalog/next.config.ts, apps/catalog/src/app/layout.tsx, apps/catalog/src/app/page.tsx, apps/catalog/src/app/api/health/route.ts, apps/catalog/src/app/api/health/route.test.ts, e2e/health.spec.ts, scripts/boot-smoke.mjs, scripts/check-compat.mjs, scripts/check-compat.test.mjs · resources: contract:toolchain, remote:github:dav033/david-ui · covers: R1 · kind: implement · subplan: SP-1 · ui: no

  Classification: complexity high; scope large_change; risk high; coupling high; confidence medium; estimate 270 minutes.
  Remote: `git init -b main` at /home/david/dev/david-ui, root commit, then `gh repo create dav033/david-ui --public --source . --push`. If `dav033/david-ui` already exists, stop as a recoverable external block naming the conflict; never delete, rename or force-push an existing remote. Nothing secret is ever committed (`.gitignore` covers `.env*`, `node_modules`, `.next`, `dist`, `.evidence/*` except `!.evidence/*.findings.json` (findings ledgers are tracked so the verifier snapshot sees them), `.vitest-cache`, `test-results`, `playwright-report`).
  Layout: root `package.json` (`private: true`, `workspaces: ["packages/*", "apps/*"]`, `engines.node >=24`, `"license": "UNLICENSED"`), `.node-version` 24. `packages/ui` is `@dav033/david-ui` version 0.0.0, `type: module`, `react`/`react-dom` 19 as peerDependencies, no Next dependency, `sideEffects: ["*.css"]`, `files: ["dist"]`, an `exports` map with one subpath per module (here `./kit-info`) whose `types` and `import` point into `dist/`; `tsconfig.build.json` compiles `src/**` (tests excluded) with tsc to per-file ESM plus `.d.ts` in `dist/`, so a leading `"use client"` survives per file. `src/kit-info.ts` exports `kitInfo()` returning `{ name: "@dav033/david-ui", version }`. `apps/catalog` is private `@david-ui/catalog`, Next 16 App Router, React 19, depending on `"@dav033/david-ui": "0.0.0"` through the workspace and importing only the package's built `exports` (like any consumer). `/api/health` answers `{ "status": "ok", "kit": kitInfo().name }`; the home page renders the kit name as plain text (no interactive elements).
  Scripts, defined once here and pointing at their producers: in `apps/catalog`, `build:next` (`next build`; deliberately not named `build`, so the verifier's per-check `npm run build --workspaces` compiles only the package; SP-6 sets the Vercel build command), `start`, `typecheck` (`next typegen && tsc --noEmit`); in `packages/ui`, `build` (tsc), `typecheck`, `catalog:check` (`node scripts/catalog-check.ts`, T4). Root: `lint` (eslint over the repo), `typecheck` (package then catalog), `test` (`vitest run`), `test:e2e` (`playwright test`), `build` (package `build`, then catalog `build:next`), `check:compat` (`node scripts/check-compat.mjs packages/ui/compat.json`), `check:deps` (`node scripts/check-deps.mjs`, T3), `catalog:check` (forwards to the package, T4), `check:kit-only` (`node scripts/check-kit-only.ts`, T5) and `verify` = lint → typecheck → test → check:compat → check:deps → catalog:check → check:kit-only → build. `verify` and the CI workflow are expected to fail until T5 lands; T6 is where they must pass. TypeScript scripts run with Node 24 native type stripping (relative imports with `.ts` extensions; the package tsconfig sets `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions`).
  Tooling: TypeScript strict in `tsconfig.base.json`; ESLint flat config with typescript-eslint, react-hooks and `@next/eslint-plugin-next` for `apps/catalog` (Next 16 has no `next lint`); Vitest with `cacheDir` `.vitest-cache` at the root (revision 9's verifier mounted `node_modules` read-only and Vitest failed with EROFS); Playwright with a `chromium` and a `chromium-reduced-motion` project and a `webServer` that builds when `apps/catalog/.next` is absent and runs `next start` on a free loopback port. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on every push to `main` and on pull requests: Node 24, `npm ci`, `npm run verify`, Playwright Chromium install and `npm run test:e2e`. README: purpose, personal use, "All rights reserved; no license is granted" and no LICENSE file (A1), workspace layout and scripts.
  `scripts/boot-smoke.mjs` builds when `.next` is absent, starts the catalog with `next start` on a free loopback port, polls `/api/health` with a 60 s deadline, asserts 200 and `kit === "@dav033/david-ui"`, requests `/` expecting 200, kills only its own process and exits nonzero on startup exit, timeout or mismatch.
  `scripts/check-compat.mjs <matrix>` (format consumed by T2): `sources` has exactly `shadcn-ui`, `animate-ui`, `bencho-ui`, `react-bits`, each with `license`, an `https` `licenseUrl` at the primary source, `retrievedAt` (YYYY-MM-DD), `publicRedistribution` (`allowed` | `forbidden` | `unclear`) and `route` (`copy-with-notice` | `clean-room` | `clean-room-or-exclude`), optional per-entry `overrides` with the same fields; `copy-with-notice` is rejected unless the verdict is `allowed`. `enhancements`: exactly 22 unique ids, each with its shadcn `base` id, `baseUiVariant` boolean and `route` (`compatible` | `manual` | `blocked` | `discarded`, the last two with a `reason`). `capabilities`: exactly 7 unique ids with `baseUiVariant`, `route` and `exposure` (`component` | `hook` | `variant` | `utility`). `notificationEngine`: one object with `engine` and `rationale`. `versions`: name → exact semver (no `^`, `~`, `*`, `x`, ranges or tags); `peerDependencies` is the only place ranges are allowed; `placement`: workspace (`root`, `packages/ui`, `apps/catalog`) → dependency and devDependency names.

  - Acceptance / static: ESLint flat config lints the package, the catalog and the scripts with zero errors. Check: `npm run lint` (authored by T1)
  - Acceptance / static: TypeScript strict type-checks the package and the catalog, including the Next route types. Check: `npm run typecheck` (authored by T1)
  - Acceptance / functional: Vitest runs the package and catalog unit tests with its cache directory outside node_modules. Check: `npm run test` (authored by T1)
  - Acceptance / functional: The compatibility validator rejects a matrix with a missing source, a wrong enhancement or capability count, a ranged version, a non-HTTPS license URL, a copy route on a source whose redistribution verdict is not allowed, or a missing or duplicated notification engine, and accepts a complete fixture. Check: `node --test scripts/check-compat.test.mjs` (authored by T1)
  - Acceptance / static: The root build compiles the package with tsc to per-file ESM with declarations and then builds the catalog with next build against it. Check: `npm run build` (authored by T1)
  - Acceptance / integration: The catalog production server starts on a free loopback port and its health route answers 200 with the kit name exported by the workspace package. Check: `node scripts/boot-smoke.mjs` (authored by T1)
  - Acceptance / functional: The Playwright health spec passes in Chromium against the catalog production server. Check: `npm run test:e2e` (authored by T1)

- [ ] T2 — License and compatibility spike: per-source redistribution verdicts, 22 enhancement and 7 capability routes on Base UI, notification engine and pinned versions · repo: app · after: T1 · verify: `npm run check:compat` · files: packages/ui/compat.json, .evidence/T2-spike.md · resources: contract:upstream-compat · covers: R2, R10, R11 · kind: research · subplan: SP-1

  Classification: complexity high; scope small_change; risk high; coupling high; confidence low; estimate 240 minutes.
  Licenses from the primary source (LICENSE file or license page, URL and retrieval date) for shadcn/ui, Animate UI, each Bencho block and React Bits Free. The verdict answers "may this code be redistributed in a public repository and a published package?": React Bits Free's MIT + Commons Clause forbids redistributing the components "alone, in a bundle, or as a ported version" (SPEC R10), so its route is `clean-room-or-exclude` (decided in SP-9); unknown or ambiguous means `unclear` and clean-room.
  For each of the 22 enhancements (inventory §4) and 7 capabilities (§5): whether Animate UI ships a Base UI variant, the install path and the candidate route; no Radix variant is ever adopted (R2).
  Notification engine (R11): Sonner versus the Animate UI toast as the single engine; record the ruling and rationale in the matrix and as a decision in the david-ui bitácora `DECISIONS.md`.
  Version matrix with exact versions for React 19, Next 16, TypeScript, Tailwind 4 and its PostCSS plugin, Base UI, Motion, the notification engine, zod (manifest schema in T4), Vitest, Testing Library, jsdom, Playwright, `@axe-core/playwright`, ESLint and its plugins, plus every npm package the 93 entries use, with each one's workspace placement. The narrative and the probes go to `.evidence/T2-spike.md`; the matrix is tracked product data that later tasks read.

  - Acceptance / static: The tracked compatibility matrix records the four source licenses with primary-source URLs and public-redistribution verdicts, the 22 enhancement routes, the 7 capability routes, exact pinned versions and one notification-engine ruling. Check: `npm run check:compat` (authored by T1)

- [ ] T3 — Install the pinned dependency set ruled by the spike and add the dependency drift check · repo: app · after: T2 · verify: `node --test scripts/check-deps.test.mjs` · files: package.json, packages/ui/package.json, apps/catalog/package.json, package-lock.json, scripts/check-deps.mjs, scripts/check-deps.test.mjs · resources: contract:dependency-set · covers: R2, R10, R11 · kind: implement · subplan: SP-1 · ui: no

  Classification: complexity medium; scope small_change; risk medium; coupling high; confidence medium; estimate 90 minutes.
  Installs every matrix package with `--save-exact` into the workspace its `placement` names. `scripts/check-deps.mjs` reads `packages/ui/compat.json`, the three `package.json` files and the installed `node_modules/<name>/package.json`, and fails on a declared package the matrix does not list, a listed package not declared, a ranged spec outside `peerDependencies`, or an installed version different from the pin; the workspace dependency `@dav033/david-ui` must equal the package version. Later tasks never edit dependency files: an entry that truly needs an unlisted package records `dependency-not-pinned:<package>` and its subplan audit sends T2/T3 back.

  - Acceptance / functional: The dependency check fails on a missing, unlisted or ranged package and on an installed version that differs from the matrix, and passes on a matching fixture. Check: `node --test scripts/check-deps.test.mjs` (authored by T3)
  - Acceptance / static: Every dependency declared by the root, package and catalog manifests is installed at the exact version the compatibility matrix pins. Check: `npm run check:deps` (authored by T3)
  - Acceptance / regression: The root build still succeeds with the full pinned dependency set installed. Check: `npm run build` (authored by T1)

- [ ] T4 — Catalog manifest with one file per entry, license register and catalog:check with exact inventory counts · repo: app · after: T3 · verify: `npm run catalog:check` · files: packages/ui/package.json, packages/ui/src/manifest/schema.ts, packages/ui/src/manifest/load.ts, packages/ui/src/manifest/index.ts, packages/ui/src/manifest/check.ts, packages/ui/src/manifest/check.test.ts, packages/ui/src/manifest/export.test.ts, packages/ui/scripts/catalog-check.ts, packages/ui/manifest/licenses.json · resources: contract:catalog-manifest · covers: R5, R10 · kind: implement · subplan: SP-1 · ui: no

  Classification: complexity high; scope full_feature; risk medium; coupling high; confidence medium; estimate 240 minutes.
  One JSON file per entry (`packages/ui/manifest/entries/<id>.json`, 93 files) and per enhancement (`packages/ui/manifest/enhancements/<id>.json`, 22 files), created by T4 but not listed in `files:` (the contract is defined by the schema, loader and check), so each later task owns only its entries' files and no shared generated index exists. `schema.ts` (zod) carries every R5 field, `applicableStates`, incorporation date, dependency-compatibility result, `ownerApproved` (default false) and clean-room provenance (`upstream: "n/a"`, consulted URL and date, license note). Seed: the 93 inventory entries `pending`, kebab-case ids, §10.3 names for Bencho (`expanding-search`, `create-menu`, `picker-wheel`, `magnifying-dock`…), priority and raw source priority per R5, and the 22 enhancements linked to their base ids with the T2 route as candidate result. `licenses.json` is the register: one record per source matching `compat.json` plus a `copiedFiles` list (empty now).
  `load.ts` reads the directory with `node:fs` and is exposed as the Node-only subpath `@dav033/david-ui/manifest` (added to the package `exports`; documented as build/server-time only). `check.ts` is a pure function returning every violation; `packages/ui/scripts/catalog-check.ts` prints them and exits nonzero.   - Acceptance / static: The catalog check accepts the seeded manifest with exactly 42 shadcn (30 P1, 12 P2), 7 capability, 12 Bencho (6 new-capability, 6 variant) and 32 React Bits (9 text, 12 ui, 6 effects, 5 backgrounds) inventory entries plus 22 linked enhancements, counting catalog-driven and own additions separately. Check: `npm run catalog:check` (authored by T4)
  - Acceptance / functional: Manifest tests reject a wrong count, a duplicate id, an enhancement without its base entry, an implemented or validated entry missing required metadata or demo, a clean-room entry without consulted URL, date and license note, a blocked or discarded entry without a reason, a copied file without its upstream license header, a register source that disagrees with the compatibility matrix, and a pending entry in final mode. Check: `npx vitest run packages/ui/src/manifest/check.test.ts` (authored by T4)
  - Acceptance / integration: The built package exports the manifest loader at @dav033/david-ui/manifest and it returns the 93 inventory entries and 22 enhancements to a Node consumer. Check: `npx vitest run packages/ui/src/manifest/export.test.ts` (authored by T4)
